I am a postdoctoral researcher in the [Computational Modeling in Psychology](https://www.lmu.de/psy/en/chairs/computational-modeling-in-psychology/) group at LMU Munich. I study how human cognition copes with complexity: how the time and memory people need grow as problems get bigger, and how people use structure and context to keep that growth in check. To answer these questions, I combine behavioral experiments and reaction-time analyses with computational models.

Beyond these topics, I am also interested in how we can make science more cumulative: For this purpose I am currently looking into how benchmarks can be used to summarise and standardise research results.

Before joining LMU, I did my PhD with Eric Schulz at the Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics and Helmholtz Munich, as part of the Max Planck School of Cognition. I also run the YouTube channel [Susanne's Scholarly Snippets](https://www.youtube.com/@SusannesScholarlySnippets), where researchers summarize their projects in a few minutes.
